identity.title: The Sample-Communication Complexity Trade-off in Federated Q-Learning

problem.claim: The paper studies Federated Q-learning, in which M agents collaboratively learn the optimal Q-function of an unknown infinite-horizon MDP with finite state and action spaces, focusing on the sample–communication trade-off for intermittent-communication algorithms.

contributions.claim: Establishes a converse lower bound: linear sample-complexity speedup in the number of agents requires communication cost at least Ω(1/(1−γ)).
Proposes Fed-DVR-Q, stated to be the first Federated Q-learning algorithm achieving order-optimal sample and communication complexities simultaneously.
Combines the converse and algorithmic results to provide a complete characterization of the sample–communication complexity trade-off.

stated_novelty.claim: Fed-DVR-Q is presented as the first Federated Q-learning algorithm to simultaneously achieve order-optimal sample and communication complexities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that any Federated Q-learning method with linear sample-complexity speedup in the number of agents must incur communication cost at least Ω(1/(1−γ)), where γ is the discount factor.
The authors report that Fed-DVR-Q simultaneously achieves order-optimal sample and communication complexities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines collaborative Federated Q-learning for finite-state, finite-action, infinite-horizon MDPs.
Focuses the analysis on the sample–communication trade-off for intermittent communication algorithms.
Provides a converse lower bound and introduces Fed-DVR-Q, which together are claimed to characterize the trade-off completely.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a converse lower bound with a constructive algorithmic result and then frames their combination as a complete trade-off characterization.

lessons.interpretation: Matching limits with an algorithm can make a complexity claim more structurally informative than presenting either result alone.
lessons.application: When studying a resource trade-off, state a necessary lower bound and design an approach that matches it under the same complexity measures.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when matching bounds are unavailable or when the lower bound and algorithm rely on incompatible assumptions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the assumptions, exact complexity definitions, or conditions under which the Ω(1/(1−γ)) lower bound and Fed-DVR-Q guarantees hold.
Details of Fed-DVR-Q and the meaning of order-optimal are not provided.
